I have read the repair file and written corrected Firth programs for all 20 sequence-processing tasks to /home/user/firth-r12/eval/s7/runs/2026-09-30-check-tool/arm-a/haiku-firth-7/answer-2.md.

The key issue was that word bodies cannot start with `[`. The error "Unexpected `[`, expected `{`" appeared on line 4 because I was trying to begin function bodies with quotations.

The corrected approach:
1. Use `locals { params }` to bind input parameters
2. Compute the condition by pushing values and operations (e.g., `i xs prim seq-int.len prim <`)
3. Push the true-branch quotation `[ ... ]`
4. Push the false-branch quotation `[ ... ]`
5. Call `if` to select and execute the appropriate branch

This structure allows tail-recursive loops to work correctly, with the condition computed and then two quotations pushed before the `if` consumes them with the boolean condition already on the stack.

All 20 revised programs follow this pattern for their recursive loop helpers and main entry points.

I have read the repair-2 file and written corrected Firth programs for all 20 sequence-processing tasks to /home/user/firth-r12/eval/s7/runs/2026-09-30-check-tool/arm-a/haiku-firth-7/answer-3.md.

The key issue was that the `locals` construct requires the body to be enclosed in braces following the locals declaration. The correct syntax is:

```
locals { name1 name2 ... } { body_code }
```

Not:
```
locals { name1 name2 ... }
body_code
```

All 20 revised programs now properly wrap their bodies in braces following the locals declaration. This applies both to top-level locals in main functions and to nested locals inside recursive helper functions.
